confirmed: The timeout is not zero. Production Connection::request callers are src/client.rs:144 (5–305 seconds, default35), src/tui.rs:73 (same bounds), src/tui.rs:112–124 (screen35seconds), and src/tui/control.rs:213,224,1570 (RPC_TIMEOUT=3seconds at line24). Client unit-test callers use2seconds. Bounds cannot overflow: min300000 precedes +5000.

Installed Rust std sys/net/connection/socket/unix.rs:385–408 converts these durations to valid timeval values. Zero duration instead produces the distinct Rust error 'cannot set a 0 duration timeout', not recorded OS errno22.

macOS peer disconnection explains the exact error with a valid35second timeout. Parent's actual socketpair probe, specs/verifications/e04s01-darwin-socket-probe.json, establishes success before peer close and errno22 after it. Apple XNU sosetoptlock rejects setsockopt with EINVAL once both SS_CANTRCVMORE and SS_CANTSENDMORE are set; UNIX-stream unp_disconnect sets these flags on both peers.

Daemon expiration is intentional, not an inferred provider behavior: README.md:132 explicitly documents that persistent clients expire after five seconds without a request, including paused/output-blocked TUI clients. src/daemon.rs:1855–1874 uses an absolute whole-frame deadline; :1905 resets it to now+5seconds before read_line, including waiting for the first byte of the next persistent request. Timeout propagates out of serve; :2077–2078 drops its result, so empty daemon.log does not disprove expiration. Reader/writer drop and ClientSlot::drop (:30–36) remove all accepted-endpoint clones.

Connection ownership has no observed fd-lifetime bug: client.rs:38–45 connects one UnixStream and creates an owned try_clone for BufReader; BufWriter owns the original. Both refer to one socket, socket options are shared, and neither endpoint is raw-closed or replaced in the TUI. Observation Connection is RefCell-owned by the main UI thread; the independent control Connection is exclusively moved into its FIFO worker.

The recorded existing ACP surface excludes initial registration failure. Native-control worker errors are caught by poll and mark disconnected (control.rs:400–429), not returned from run. Observation failures can escape via snapshot polling (tui.rs:868), through run to main.rs:2–4 and exit1. ACP-inspect errors at tui.rs:840–843 are displayed/caught; subsequent snapshot failure is fatal. For the recorded still-active ACP view, the native-screen path is skipped. Failing set_read_timeout occurs before request serialization/write, so that particular failing request was not sent.

parent_runtime_experiment.purpose: Discriminate harness-induced starvation without modifying src/client.rs or changing production deadline/error handling.
steps: Run the same synthetic private ACP smoke under a persistent private Zsh host, but start a dedicated PTY master reader before launching the TUI and keep it alive independently across every Eval return, tool call, daemon-state wait, and assertion. Follow existing Attachment/drain_outer: bounded retained capture but continue draining after retention cap; never hold the screen/capture lock across file I/O or parent waits.

Repeat API total42 then native human total57. After57, deliberately leave the foreground driver idle for longer than five seconds while the independent drainer remains running. Record drainer heartbeat/bytes and TUI liveness; then type a distinctive local draft, capture it, and exercise subsequent ownership steps. Keep daemon/host/reader cleanup private and explicit.

If it still fails while continuously drained, capture the live UI thread stack before releasing/reaping it. A stack inside terminal write/draw distinguishes output blockage; a live event/RPC stack shifts investigation. At the timeout failure, temporary diagnostic instrumentation should preserve original errno first, then record timeout seconds/nanoseconds, reader/writer fd, request caller/type, fcntl F_GETFD/F_GETFL, getsockopt SO_TYPE, poll revents and non-consuming recv(MSG_PEEK|MSG_DONTWAIT). Do not use SO_ERROR (clears pending error), consume stream bytes, retry requests, or alter timeout.

To establish the daemon-side reason if needed, parent can temporarily retain serve's error plus connection ID and elapsed-last-frame time instead of discarding it at daemon.rs:2078; distinguish client-frame deadline/read WouldBlock from response write timeout. No permanent diagnostics/workaround recommended.
